4c1bd1aa6b2e47f12ad7d38e747f5a0723ac1cfd.summary: WikiLeaks published the source code and development logs for Hive on 9 November 2017. The text describes Hive as a major CIA component for controlling its malware, providing covert communications between implants and operators. Operations use cover domains and rented relay servers that pass traffic over a VPN to a hidden CIA server. The page is a repost of that release and was archived on 2026-11-25.

4c46fb4b612355eadc79e8b39041441329d772c5.summary: Jamf Threat Labs describes CloudSyncD, a two-stage macOS backdoor delivered as a fake Zoom installer. The first stage uses a fake authorization prompt to capture the user's password, hides it in a decoy configuration file using zero-width characters, and then launches a second-stage implant that beacons to a command-and-control server. The first sample was seen on September 15, 2026, in a development build; later builds were configured against live infrastructure. The report did not observe persistence being established.

4ca9538e60f7b82ccc9f00a6ae6070efe90afd2f.summary: Sysdig's Threat Research Team describes JADEPUFFER, an operator whose extortion campaign was driven end-to-end by a large language model. It entered an internet-facing Langflow server through CVE-2025-3248, harvested credentials, and moved to a production database server running Alibaba Nacos and MySQL. It took over the Nacos configuration service, encrypted 1,342 configuration items, left a ransom note, and dropped databases. The report says the evidence points to an autonomous agent, but it cannot confirm the exfiltration claim or the origin of the wallet.

4cc0024b221effc8ae71cd54f6391a929ecbacf1.summary: BleepingComputer reports that a cyberattack on UnitedHealth subsidiary Optum disrupted the Change Healthcare payment platform. Unnamed sources linked it to the BlackCat (ALPHV) ransomware gang, which had not claimed it at publication; the article could not confirm this. UnitedHealth's SEC filing described suspected nation-state hackers. Sources also named an exploited ScreenConnect flaw, CVE-2024-1709. The article gives background on BlackCat's activity and the FBI's disruption of its leak sites.
